title.narrative: Overall objective

description.narrative: Supporting Evidence of Achievement:Health Impact Mitigation:Nationwide vaccination campaign implemented, prioritising vulnerable and highrisk groups.Infodemic risks reduced and vaccine adherence improved through risk communication and multilingual campaigns.COVID19 prevention and control measures implemented at all levels, including in nonCOVID health services.System Strengthening:Support to strategic planning (PNDS, PESIS), digital systems (DHIS2), and supply quantification (WHO EFT).Deployment of trained IPC focal points, surveillance officers, and data analysts at municipal and provincial levels.Support to the Health Observatory and integration of COVID19 and routine health information systems.Continuity of Essential Health Services:Guidelines, training, supervision, and outreach ensured routine services (e.g. maternal, HIV, chronic care) remained available despite pandemic disruptions.Monitoring of performance indicators, mitigation of lowperforming programmes, and rollout of resilience strategies.Conclusion: The Action effectively mitigated the health and systemic effects of COVID19 in Angola, strengthened institutional and municipal capacities, and maintained essential health services thereby fully meeting the overall objective.

title.narrative: O.2. Support the provision of targeted integrated package to prevent COVID19 and reduce the associated health impact

description.narrative: The project achieved this output by supporting the delivery of integrated, multisectoral health interventions targeting both prevention and continuity of care.Integration of COVID19 with Essential Health Services:WHO supported the revision and dissemination of operational guidelines to integrate COVID19 response within essential services (e.g. maternal and child health, HIV, TB).Trained health workers to deliver care in a way that preserved continuity of services during COVID19 surges.Support to COVID19 Case Management and IPC (Infection Prevention and Control):Distributed Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), oxygen therapy supplies, and diagnostic kits.Supported training of clinicians and hospital staff in COVID19 case management protocols, including severe and critical care.Deployment of Field Epidemiologists and IPC Specialists:WHO deployed technical teams to hightransmission provinces to support outbreak control and ensure the integration of public health measures with clinical and logistical support.Targeted Outreach Campaigns:Coordinated with provincial health departments to conduct mobile clinics and community outreach, targeting underserved populations.Promoted risk communication on COVID19 alongside messaging on MNCH, immunization, and chronic disease care.Strengthening Referral Systems:Supported improvements in referral mechanisms for COVID19 and nonCOVID conditions, particularly at municipal level.Helped reorganise service delivery in a way that reduced crossinfection while maintaining access to care.These combined actions demonstrate that WHO successfully supported an integrated prevention and response package that reduced COVID19 impact while safeguarding other health services, as required under Output O.2.

title.narrative: O.3. Mitigate the disruption of essential services to reduce vulnerability to SARSCoV2 infection

description.narrative: The project actively addressed the disruption of essential services during the pandemic, aiming to maintain access and reduce health system vulnerabilities.Evaluation of Service Disruption and Gaps:WHO supported the evaluation of the PNDS 20122025, identifying disruptions in routine services during COVID19.This informed corrective planning through the design of the new Strategic Health Plan (PNDS 20232027), which included measures to ensure service continuity during public health emergencies.Operational Guidelines for Continuity of Care:Updated and disseminated guidelines for maintaining essential services (e.g. maternal & child health, HIV, chronic diseases) during COVID19 outbreaks.These included specific protocols for safe service delivery, triage, and referral in the context of infection prevention and control (IPC).Support to Provincial and Municipal Health Directorates:Strengthened subnational planning capacities to adjust services according to transmission scenarios.Provided technical assistance, training, and supervision to ensure adaptability of services during waves of infection.Field Deployments and Mobile Interventions:Deployed WHOsupported teams and experts to priority provinces to support outreach services and maintain critical care coverage.Facilitated mobile health units and decentralised service delivery, particularly in hardtoreach and urban poor communities.Strengthening Information Systems to Monitor Disruptions:Reinforced DHIS2 with new performance indicators to monitor the continuity of essential services in real time.Reactivated the Health Observatory, providing analytical oversight of essential health service trends.These measures show that the project successfully mitigated service disruption risks and contributed to maintaining essential services during the pandemic, fulfilling Output O.3.

title.narrative: 3.1 Performance indicators of essential health services are monitored

description.narrative: The project successfully implemented activities to monitor the performance of essential health services.Integration with Health Information Systems (DHIS2):WHO supported the updating and standardisation of indicators within the DHIS2 platform, Angolas main digital health monitoring tool.Performance indicators for essential services (e.g. MNCH, HIV, COVID19) were integrated and streamlined for regular monitoring.Development of SOPs and Monitoring Tools:Standard Operating Procedures and monitoring & evaluation frameworks were developed.These guided data collection at municipal and provincial levels and improved data consistency and reporting frequency.Evaluation of Routine Service Delivery (PNDS & PESIS):WHO supported the evaluation of the PNDS (20122025) and PESIS (20152022).The evaluations assessed delivery and continuity of essential health services, identifying service gaps and proposing updated indicators for the next cycle.Support to National Health Observatory:The reactivation and support to the Health Observatory facilitated the systematic analysis and publication of health performance data.These activities confirm that essential service performance was actively monitored, and monitoring systems were improved, meeting the expectations under Output 3.1.

title.narrative: 3.2 Lowperformance programmes are identified and effects of disruption are mitigated

description.narrative: This output has been achieved, with concrete evidence of both identification and mitigation.Support to PNDS Evaluation and Strategic PlanningThe National Health Development Plan (PNDS) 20122025 was evaluated in detail.This evaluation identified lowperformance areas, including weaknesses in continuity of essential services during the pandemic.Design of the new PNDS 20232027Based on the findings above, WHO supported the Ministry of Health in redefining priority programmes and aligning them with updated epidemiological trends.This directly addressed the disruption of routine services by proposing corrective measures and reprogramming efforts.Review of Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health (MNCH) and HIV programmesThe project supported evaluations and updated operational guidelines to safeguard vulnerable services during COVID19 surges.This included continuity strategies, integration into emergency planning, and targeted resource allocations.Health Systems Resilience Strategy (under preparation)WHO initiated the drafting of a longterm Health Systems Resilience Strategy in partnership with MINSA, building on lessons from disruptions.These actions demonstrate that underperforming programmes were not only identified but also systematically addressed, fulfilling Output 3.2 as planned.

title.narrative: 5.1.Analysis and strategic data on routine health information are generated

description.narrative: This output was achieved and documented.Evaluation of the Strategic Plan for the Health Information System (PESIS 20152022)A full evaluation was carried out by a WHOrecruited consultant.Findings were used to inform drafting of the new Strategic Plan 20232027 for health information systems.Development of SOPs and M&E frameworks for DHIS2SOPs were created to improve consistency and data flows.The project supported the development of interoperable digital platforms to integrate health data systems.Provision of IT equipment and trainingEquipment was delivered to strengthen data management capacity.Trainings were conducted at central and provincial levels (e.g., for municipal directors and technicians).Reactivation and support to National Health ObservatoryThe project contributed to institutional frameworks for routine data analysis and dissemination.Analytical reports and data dashboards were made available.Support to COVID19 data integration with broader health planningCOVID19 surveillance data were incorporated into the national planning and quantification tools (linked to Output 5.2).These combined actions clearly confirm that routine health data is now systematically collected, analysed, and used for strategic planning in line with Output 5.1.

title.narrative: 5.2 Quantification of needs in COVID19 health products and essential medicines is informed by reliable morbidity and mortality data

description.narrative: This output was achieved through the use of forecasting tools, improved surveillance data, and nationallevel coordination mechanisms.Use of WHO Essential Forecasting Tool (EFT):The WHO Essential Forecasting Tool (v4) was deployed to estimate national and subnational needs using realtime surveillance data.It was used for the quantification, procurement, and supply management of COVID19 commodities and essential medicines, including oxygen.Capacity Building and Simulation Exercises:UNDP, WHO, and MINSA staff (especially GEPE technicians) were trained in Q4 2021 to conduct quarterly quantification exercises by province.A simulation scenario based on a Variant of Concern resurgence was used during the training to enhance readiness.Integration of Surveillance and Mortality Data:The tool relied on routine morbidity and mortality surveillance data, aligned with DHIS2 and updated national epidemiological reports.This ensured that quantification reflected actual burden and trends, including provinciallevel variations.Adhoc Quantification During Variant Surges:The system allowed for flexible, realtime quantification during periods of increased transmission or new variant emergence, ensuring rapid response capacity.These efforts confirm that reliable morbidity and mortality data directly informed the quantification of COVID19 health products, fully achieving Output 5.2.

title.narrative: 1.1The vaccination campaign is implemented at the entire national territory within the established timeline covering risk groups, vulnerable population and potential new risk groups due to Variants of Concern

description.narrative: This output was fully achieved, with evidence of nationallevel rollout, risk group prioritisation, and timeline adherence.Nationwide Rollout of COVID19 Vaccination:The campaign was successfully implemented across all 18 provinces of Angola.WHO provided continuous technical and logistical support through the National Interministerial Vaccination Task Force and provincial coordination mechanisms.Prioritisation of Risk and Vulnerable Groups:The campaign focused on healthcare workers, elderly populations, people with comorbidities, and frontline workers.Later phases included adolescents and other vulnerable groups, as per the evolving Strategic Vaccination Plan.Response to Variants of Concern (VoCs):WHO supported reprogramming of vaccination strategies in response to new VoCs and changing transmission patterns.Booster campaigns were implemented targeting newly identified highrisk groups.Cold Chain and Supply Management:Cold chain capacity was strengthened at national and provincial levels to accommodate various vaccine types.WHO assisted with distribution planning, stock management, and vaccine safety monitoring.Monitoring & Adherence to Timeline:The campaign was carried out within the expected timeframe, aligned with national targets and COVAX distribution schedules.WHO provided field monitoring, data collection support, and coordination for midcourse corrections when needed.These combined efforts confirm that the vaccination campaign was implemented nationally, on schedule, and with adaptive prioritisation to emerging risks and vulnerable groups fully achieving Output 1.1.

title.narrative: O.1. Support to implementing the COVID19 vaccination campaign

description.narrative: This was one of the core components of the Action, and the report confirms significant achievements in supporting Angolas COVID19 vaccination efforts.Technical Support to the National Vaccination Task Force:WHO provided strategic and operational support to the Interministerial Vaccination Task Force, including coordination, planning, and technical advice for vaccine rollout.Support to Cold Chain and Logistics:Delivered cold chain equipment, including refrigerators and freezers, to several provinces.Assisted in the mapping of cold chain capacity at national and subnational levels.Supported the development of distribution plans for vaccines, syringes, and safety boxes.Training of Health Workers:Facilitated training sessions for vaccinators and logistics staff, including safe handling, reporting of adverse events, and data entry into the electronic vaccination system.Monitoring & Supervision of Vaccination Campaigns:WHO participated in and supported joint field missions with MINSA to monitor campaign progress.Provided realtime technical assistance during surge periods (especially in Luanda and Huambo).Risk Communication & Community Engagement (RCCE):Developed and disseminated communication materials to combat vaccine hesitancy and misinformation.Mobilized community leaders and civil society to support local vaccination campaigns.Support to Digital Vaccination Registry:Provided input on improving the digital registry and reporting systems for COVID19 vaccination data.Helped align digital tools with DHIS2 and national health information systems.These efforts confirm that WHO played a central role in coordinating, scaling, and sustaining Angolas COVID19 vaccination campaign, meeting the expectations under Output O.1.
